qal-definition-replace-model-with-qnn: Section I, p.1: the paper states what it takes QAL to be, replacing the classical model by a QNN in the active-learning workflow. The passage cites [29] only for a related experiment
qal-contribution-statement: Section I, p.2: the paper states its own contribution, QAL in the gate-model paradigm with equivariant deep QNNs
qal-uncertainty-sampling-defn: Section II.A, p.2: describes USAMP as mapping the model to P_theta and, for binary tasks, querying the sample nearest fifty-fifty. A known strategy, cited to [42], but stated here as the strategy the paper uses
qal-def1-least-confidence: Definition 1, Section II.A, p.2, Eq. (1): argmax of 1 minus the probability of the most probable label
qal-def2-margin-sampling: Definition 2, Section II.A, p.2, Eq. (2): argmin of the gap between the two most likely labels; the 'small margin is ambiguous' reason is in the next sentence
qal-def3-entropy-sampling: Definition 3, Section II.A, p.2, Eq. (3): argmax of the entropy of the predicted class distribution
qal-def4-voting-entropy: Definition 4, Section II.A, p.3, Eq. (4): committee vote-share entropy, V(y_j) the votes for a class
qal-def5-density-weighted: Definition 5, Section II.A, p.3, Eq. (5): largest average similarity to the other pool samples; the combination remark is in the next sentence
qal-def-label-invariance-quantum: Section II.C, p.3 to 4, Eq. (8): f(U rho U dagger) = f(rho) = y for all rho of label y and every U in G. The formula is in the text layer after the quoted words
qal-def-gate-invariance: Definition 7, Section II.C, p.4, Eq. (14): the gate is equivariant iff it commutes with R_q(g) for all theta and all g in S
qal-def-twirling-formula: Definition 8, Section II.C, p.4, Eq. (15): the twirl averages R(g) G R dagger(g) over S, commutes with each R(g), and gives the equivariant gate exp(-i theta T_R[G])
qal-donut-dataset-setup: Figure 3 caption, p.5: 500 samples, Gaussian radius, uniform angle, label by the sign of cos(2 theta + 0.58), 3:1:1 split
qal-eqnn-z-three-params-per-layer: Section III.B, p.5, Eqs. (17) to (19): RZ and RXX gates from generators unchanged by the Z tensor Z twirl, giving 3d parameters for d layers
qal-encoder-breaks-swap-pseudosymmetry: Section III.B, p.5: the RX and RY order differs on the two qubits to break the SWAP pseudo-symmetry; the same-expectation consequence is stated in the next sentences
qal-hea-baseline-design: Section III.B, p.6, Eq. (20): two RX gates outside the equivariant set plus a CNOT, same measured operator, trained as a baseline to validate GQML
qal-donut-training-setup: Section III.C, p.6: binary cross-entropy, Adam at 0.1, 100 epochs, no batching, uniform init in [-pi, pi], best validation accuracy in history selects the model

qal-ttt-encoding-9-qubits-onehot: Section IV.B, p.8: one-hot encoding, one qubit per site, RX angle 2 pi g_i / 3 with g_i in {+1, -1, 0}, D4 acting as SWAPs on the 9-qubit grid
qal-ttt-network-config-l2-d5: Section IV.B, p.8: (l, d) = (2, 5) in the numerical experiments, with the layer string and the corner, middle and edge observables in Eqs. (25) to (27)
qal-ttt-training-setup-mse: Section IV.C, p.9: MSE loss, Adam at 0.1, 200 epochs, no batching, and the stated reason for MSE over cross-entropy
qal-limit-mitigation-out-of-scope: Section V, p.10: exploring QAL strategies that mitigate the biased sampling 'goes beyond the scope of this study'
qal-code-availability-mindspore-quantum: Code Availability, p.11: the authors state they used MindSpore Quantum and provide codes, datasets and results in a repository. This records what they state, not that the repository was checked
qal-two-scenarios-setup: Section V, p.10: the methodology is exemplified in two scenarios, slicing-a-donut with Z2 and tic-tac-toe with D4
restaurant-game-rules: The Restaurant Game section, p.3, Eq. (1): n restaurants, one closed at random, Eve knows the strategy but not the private channel, conditions (h1) p(y=x|x) = 0 and (h2) sum over x of p(y|x)p(x) = 1/n

restaurant-ten-games-setup: Results, p.3: ten H3 games, PPBS vertical split ratio 1/3, probabilities from detected-photon ratios, about 4800 photons per experiment

restaurant-classical-optimum-by-discreti: Supplement II.D, p.16 to 17: E_C comes from a linear program per distribution p_A, minimum taken, by discretizing p_A; the 10^-3 precision is the paper's statement about LP algorithms in general, as the value reports
restaurant-prop3-certification: Proposition 3, Supplement III, p.18: proved in the paper by showing orthogonal encodings and projective measurements are each classically simulable with one bit, so advantage needs coherence and a non-projective measurement. No outside theorem is used
restaurant-device-certification-protocol: Supplement III, p.17 to 18: the verifier compares E_V with E_C and confirms quantumness if E_V < E_C, otherwise certification fails; the paper defines this protocol
restaurant-games-on-curve-gamma: Supplement II.C, p.16: PPBS reflection ratio 1/3 and ten games on the curve Gamma of Eq. (41)

theory_low.restaurant-prop1-robust-advantage: Proposition 1, Supplement I.C, p.13: the statement rests on an assumption that the noisy quantum index tends to zero with the noise, and on Proposition 2 for continuity; the argument is not written out in full
theory_low.restaurant-prop2-min-continuous: Proposition 2, Supplement I.C, p.14: stated for any continuous f with no domain condition, so the conditions are lost; the proof assumes a minimizer exists. True only on a compact domain, which the statement does not say
theory_low.restaurant-polarimeter-arbitrary-pov-m-e: Supplement II.B, p.16: a design argument, not a theorem with stated conditions; the rank-1 proof text is partly missing from the text layer

value_replace.qrc-g3-family-optimal-design: The author reports, for seven circuit families used as reservoirs to predict excited energies of LiH and H2O, that families with higher majorization complexity perform better and the G3 family gives the lowest error, with MG slightly worse and the Ising model similar; the author calls G3 the optimal design also because MG gates are harder to implement and the Ising circuits need far more gates.

qrc-g3-family-optimal-design: predicting the excited energies of the electronic Hamiltonian of two molecules, LiH and H2O, given their ground state.
